note: A sea backdrop places areas on the sea-level datum instead of the void one, so it is a different world for the same campaign and cannot coexist with `void`. It builds from the SHORE set — the same hall and the same annex tiles lifted onto two courses of plinth, with a tide pool cut into the floor course so each piece's top water block lands on the sea plane and `waterline_y` can say so (`DW0344`). The unlifted pieces stand their walk plane at y=61, a block under a sea at 62, and vanilla waterlogs every waterloggable block the placement puts there: booted on the pinned server that world came up with 10 waterlogged blocks and 367 water cells across the hall's floor. It is also the only point of this domain where the three sea proofs have anything to look at: `validation/fluid-escape.json` (`DW0318`, water that leaves the built volume), `validation/sea-seepage.json` (`DW0851`, the sea in the walk region, measured over every walk cell) and the `DW0344` waterline binding all ship here with real denominators.
